title: Finish this sentence: “If nothing stopped me, this year I'd…”
why: Imagining your best possible future makes it feel more reachable.

title: Spend 20 minutes on something you loved as a kid. Rate your energy after, 1 to 5.
why: Old loves are clues to what still lights you up.

title: Pick one value, like curiosity, courage or kindness, and do one thing today that shows it.
why: Living by your values, in small acts, is what makes a life feel meaningful.

title: Do the first lesson of a skill you keep saying you'll learn.
why: Starting is the hardest part, and one lesson is a real start.

title: Make something and show one person: a page, a sketch, a recipe, a song.
why: Sharing what you make turns a hobby into a thread of meaning.

title: Decide when and where you'll do your next Purpose quest: “At [time] in [place], I will…”
why: A specific plan beats willpower.

title: Write down one thing you made progress on today, however small.
why: Noticing progress, even tiny progress, is a big source of motivation.

title: Name your top three values in one word each. Circle the one you lived least this week.
why: Knowing your values makes the next meaningful choice easier to spot.

title: Finish this sentence: “On a free Saturday with nobody watching, I'd…”
why: Your answers when nobody's grading point at what truly matters to you.

title: Pick a goal you care about and do a first step so small it takes 2 minutes. Then do it.
why: Tiny starts lower the barrier, and progress fuels the next step.

title: Ask yourself: “When did I last lose track of time?” Write down the answer.
why: The moments you get absorbed in are clues to what fits you.

title: Message someone whose work you admire and tell them one thing it taught you.
why: Saying it means more to them than you'd guess, and it sharpens your own direction.

title: Write the headline you'd love to read about yourself one year from now.
why: Imagining a future where things went well makes it feel more reachable.

title: Cross one thing off your list that doesn't matter to you. Drop it, delay it or hand it off.
why: Room for what matters often starts with a small no to what doesn't.

title: Write for 15 minutes about your best possible life five years from now. Be specific.
why: Picturing your best possible self lifts mood and makes goals feel more real.

title: Set a 25-minute timer and work on the project you keep postponing. Stop when it rings.
why: A short, defined burst makes starting easier, and starting is the hard part.

title: Write for 10 minutes about a value you care about and a time you lived it.
why: Reflecting on your values helps you stay steady when things get stressful.

title: Teach a friend something you know well, in 20 minutes or less.
why: Explaining what you know shows you how much you've grown, and deepens it.

title: Take a 20-minute walk with one question in mind: “What do I want more of this year?”
why: Walking gets ideas moving. People think more creatively on their feet.

title: Look back at your week: list what gave you energy and what drained it. Plan one more of the first.
why: Your energy is data about what suits you.

title: Volunteer for a half day with a cause you care about.
why: Giving time to something bigger than you is one of the surest sources of meaning.

title: Finish one small creative project in an afternoon: a zine, a short song, a series of sketches.
why: Starting and finishing a whole thing in one go feels great, and it's flow fuel.

title: Spend three hours on a skill you want. Find the hardest part and practice just that.
why: Focused practice on the hard parts is how skill really grows.

title: Interview someone who has a job you're curious about. Bring three questions.
why: Talking to people who do the thing beats guessing from the outside.

title: Plan your next three months on one page: one goal, three steps, a date for each.
why: Clear goals with set times are far likelier to happen.

title: Put one thing out there: enter a contest, publish a post, send a pitch or an application.
why: Sharing your work is how it becomes real, and each try builds confidence.

title: Go to a talk, workshop or meetup in a field you're curious about, and ask one question.
why: New people in new fields are where surprising opportunities come from.

title: Set up a skill swap: you teach a friend one thing, they teach you one thing back.
why: Teaching and learning side by side grows both people.
